s: 'Perantaallu' means
o: A sati practice in Kakatiya period
An evil social practice of Telugu Choda times
Women who committed sati were elevated to the status of demi goddesses and were worshipped as perantallu during the rule of Reddis in Andhra

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet who translated the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Telugu as ' Andhra Mahabharatam '.
II. He is also credited with writing ' Andhra Shabda Chintamani ', a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.
III. Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya.
x:
Official key: I and III (Nandampudi to Nannaya). Strictly: the Nandampudi grant names Narayana Bhattu as donee and Nannaya as its composer, so I and II (NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.20, p.33).
Statements I and II are right: Nannaya translated the Mahabharata (Andhra Mahabharatam) and is credited with Andhra Shabda Chintamani. Statement III is wrong, because Rajaraja Narendra gave Nandampudi to Narayana Bhattu and Nannaya only composed the grant (official key: I and III).

s: Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra?
x:
Some keys: Basava (founder of Veerashaivism) or Somanatha (who popularised it in Telugu). Strictly: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya propagated it in Andhra (NextGen Andhra Cholas p.3).
Veerashaivism was spread in Andhra by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya (12th c.); Basava founded it in Karnataka, and Palkuriki Somanatha later popularised it through Telugu literature. The printed key (Basava) contradicts its own explanation.

s: Telugu literature was first influenced by which empire?
x:
Key: Vijayanagara Empire. Strictly: Telugu literature began under the Eastern Chalukyas (Nannaya); Vijayanagara gave its golden age.
